variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONE NEW three-view concept of the RH PIRATE LIGHT FIGHTER from Freelancer, based on the ACTUAL original ship. This is a test redesign for the user's Junker/scavenger faction. Make a thoughtful authored redesign with changed hull planes and integrated donor housings, not simply repainting or tracing the old mesh. Preserve original identity, cabin and mechanism.

REFERENCE ROLES:
IMAGE 1: ACTUAL native rh_pir_fighter, all FLIGHT views. Authoritative proportions and masses.
IMAGE 2: IMMUTABLE original rh_pir_fighter CABIN closeups. It is a different cabin from the freighter or elite. Preserve this exact module.
IMAGE 3: ACTUAL wing mechanism at FLIGHT, halfway, STOWED, front and top. Design compatible two-piece wings, but the final art sheet uses FLIGHT only.
IMAGE 4: historical Rheinland fighter design, for the characteristic low blunt nose, sloping neck, upright aft circular mass and angular contrasts. Ignore the sketch's different cabin, green paint, weapons and arrow.
IMAGE 5: actual pirate fighter material atlas: worn pale metal, inset red salvage panels and subdued olive donor fields. Use meaningful panel placement; do not copy military crosses.

MAIN FORM:
A compact narrow fighter, original flight dimensions approximately W10.915 H7.125 L13.606. Low forward ORIGINAL cabin; short boxy sloping neck/spine rising behind it; strong elevated circular DRUM at the AFT body; exactly ONE CENTRAL REAR ENGINE / ONE axial exhaust. The aft circular disk has its broad round sides facing PORT and STARBOARD, not forward like a turbine fan. It is a thick but transversely NARROW vertical mass, visibly round in SIDE, narrow along the centerline in TOP. Preserve the contrast of circular rear housing and angular neck; do not turn it into a long freighter, ball, giant barrel, wide pod, modern streamlined jet or flat airplane. Keep the original relative cabin size and original location. Closed integrated transitions between masses. A compact solid dorsal shoulder at the drum base may be reshaped, but no open exterior beams.

IMMUTABLE FIGHTER CABIN:
Copy image 2 closely, whole module unchanged: tall blunt faceted downward-hanging nose; large slanted blue FRONT windshield with a lower blue band just below its narrow yellow-black division; tall triangular/trapezoidal SIDE panes separated by original broad metal frames; small overhanging brow; lower opaque stepped metal chin with the original small blue corner slots and dark-red side inset; yellow-black bumper band and small tapered underside tip. It is NOT the freighter's cabin and NOT an elite canopy. No new glazing geometry, pilot bubble, continuous all-glass lower nose or cockpit armour. Keep complete original size and shape. Design the new neck around it. Later modeling will reuse the actual cabin mesh, UV and cockpit resources.

WINGS / MECHANICS:
Exactly TWO SHORT WING ASSEMBLIES, one each side beneath the middle neck, each with an INNER SLIDING SECTION and OUTER HINGED SECTION. FLIGHT geometry follows image 1 and the first column of image 3: forward-swept angular wings in TOP, tips slightly AHEAD of roots; wings droop down/outward in front/3/4, with outer sections aligned with inner span. Keep similar original span and chord, no huge sweeping bomber wings, no tiny fins. Wing surface is closed with meaningful thickness, an inset panel and a clear elbow joint; not a truss or ribbed skeleton.
The current native mechanism slides inner sections inward/upward/backward when stowing, while outer panels roll UP around the fore-aft hinge axis through about 63 degrees. Allow space for that sweep and sliding root; do not weld across the elbow or surround it with immovable armour. All three final views depict the same FLIGHT state, no stowed wings mixed into the sheet.
Aft large drum and central engine are FIXED; do NOT make them rotate like the freighter roof. A distinct longitudinal sliding CARGO LID sits on top of the neck just behind the cabin, opening by sliding AFT about 3.37 units. Keep a purposeful rectangular inset lid and clear rearward pocket. Show it CLOSED. No round roof cargo shutter.

PIRATE DESIGN AND DETAIL:
Authentic Freelancer industrial scavenger redesign. Angular structural replacement panels, shifted closed housings, purposeful diagonal joints, sculpted solid shoulder transitions, one or two deep closed-backed ventilation pockets with a few broad blades. Moderate meaningful medium-scale detail: two or three varied inset service fields along neck/shoulder, one large inset field on the drum side subdivided into a few broad sectors, shaped single-engine collar, substantial closed wing-root sockets. Leave calm readable planes between these. Geometry should remain interesting after fine texture is removed. No dense tiny boxes, geometric rivets, fine grids or dozens of fasteners. Pirate character from physical donor construction, not just a different color. No national flag or Rheinland cross, no huge skull, no attached weapons. Keep hardpoint landing areas unobstructed.
NO exposed pipes, hoses, cables; NO exterior frames, open trusses, diagonal braces, cages or skeletal pylons. Do not use disconnected primitives as decoration. Recesses are closed at back. No generic rounding/bevels on every angular hull edge. Retain deliberately circular drum silhouette and crisp hull/wing tips.

PAGE:
Exactly THREE coherent views of the same redesigned fighter on off-white concept paper: large front-side 3/4 LEFT, true SIDE / FLIGHT upper RIGHT nose RIGHT, true TOP / FLIGHT lower RIGHT nose UP. Clear full uncropped silhouettes. Same cockpit, wing geometry, single rear engine and aft drum between views. Refined ink with controlled marker/gouache shading, geometric readable surfaces, restrained worn pale grey/beige, muted dark red and a little olive. No environment, no exploded parts, no extra inset. Titles only as specified plus SIDE / FLIGHT and TOP / FLIGHT.

SPECIFIC F01 DESIGN: Close to the native overall proportions. Rebuild the neck as a single sloping angular box with a stepped lower edge, one large trapezoidal inset red side field and a compact deep vent behind it. Keep the rear drum strongly round; replace its outer side skin with three or four broad reclaimed angular sectors wrapped around one deep circular inset, a robust closed crescent lower housing integrated into the neck, and an unbroken circular back silhouette. The nose-facing drum shoulder is a short solid shaped transition, no open bar. The ONE engine has a short compact faceted aft collar. Wings remain fairly straight/angular and forward-swept like source, with clipped sharp outer tips, one distinct inset red panel per inner wing and broad quiet pale outer panels. Short purposeful root sliders and hinge elbows. Medium detail, no clutter. Keep original low cabin especially faithful. Title exactly: RH JUNKER FIGHTER / F01
